samples.summary: Text-op history presence still publishes `{blockId, offset}` with no affinity, so redo restores a wrap-boundary caret with the wrong reading
samples.evidence: `recordHistoryPresence` was widened to `DocPosition`, but the text/structural mutation call sites still hand it a freshly built narrow position: `recordHistoryPresence(p, { blockId, offset: offset + text.length })` (insertText, line 1651), `{ blockId, offset }` (deleteText, 1730), `{ blockId, offset: offset + 1 }` (1574), `{ blockId: newBlockId, offset: 0 }` (splitBlock, 2113), `{ blockId, offset: mergeOffset }` (mergeBlocks, 2300). Yorkie re-applies these post-edit presence values on **redo**, so redoing a typing edit whose caret lands exactly on a wrap boundary restores `activeCursorPos` without `lineAffinity`; the editor's redo path (`packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2067`) then spreads that affinity-less position into `cursor.moveTo`, which defaults to `'backward'` and re-collapses the caret onto the previous visual line — the exact failure mode this change claims to close. The comment added in `packages/frontend/src/types/users.ts:25` ("re-published by `recordHistoryPresence` on every edit") is therefore only true for style/structural ops that pass `cursorForHistory` through. The new frontend test deliberately exercises `applyStyle` only, so nothing covers the text-op path.
searchedFor: grep recordHistoryPresence( in yorkie-doc-store.ts with -B6 (all 20+ call sites)

samples.summary: `moveTo` no longer normalizes affinity, so a stale pre-delete affinity now rides onto the post-delete caret
samples.evidence: `deleteSelection` ends with `this.cursor.moveTo(start)` (also line 3384) where `start` is the normalized selection start. Selection endpoints legitimately carry `lineAffinity` (see `selection.ts:260`, `text-editor.ts:2778`/`2813`, and the mouse path at `text-editor.ts:1521-1525`), so `start` can carry `'forward'`. Before this change `moveTo(pos)` forced `'backward'`, normalizing away any endpoint affinity; now `moveTo` inherits `pos.lineAffinity`. The affinity was computed against the pre-deletion line layout, and the deletion reflows the block, so if the surviving offset is still a wrap boundary the caret is drawn at the start of the following visual line instead of at the deletion point — and that stale reading is what gets published to presence. The same inheritance applies to the arrow-key collapse path `this.cursor.moveTo(collapsePos)` (line 2789) and to the clamped undo/redo restores `{...restoredPos, offset: Math.min(restoredPos.offset, maxOffset)}` (`editor.ts:2035`, `2067`), where the affinity is kept even when `Math.min` moved the offset to a completely different place in the block.
searchedFor: read model/document.ts deleteBackward (returns the caller's `pos` object in three branches)

samples.summary: Peer-cursor change detection key omits `lineAffinity`, so an affinity-only peer move does not refresh the label timer
samples.evidence: `const posKey = `${presence.activeCursorPos.blockId}:${presence.activeCursorPos.offset}`;` — now that peer caret rendering honours `lineAffinity` (editor.ts:1570), a peer whose caret changes only its wrap-boundary reading (same blockId/offset, e.g. Home vs. End on a wrapped line) moves visually by one line but is treated as unchanged, so the name label is not re-shown. Cosmetic only.
